title: Choose the stats site's structure
question: Three structures for the public Mat Stats site, all in the existing dark ledger look. Lock one.

options.label: Tale of the tape
options.thesis: Rankings on the left; pick any two rows and a pre-fight tale of the tape builds beside them.
options.viewport: Athlete rankings with quality filters fill the left; a sticky comparison column on the right compares two picked athletes or teams, figure by figure.
options.risk: The comparison column is empty until two rows are picked, so it needs a good default (the top two).

options.label: Belt standings board
options.thesis: The home page as standings: a top-seven table per belt, like weight-class rankings, with top teams and the latest events under them.
options.viewport: A summary row (athletes, teams, events, matches read), then four belt columns of ranked athletes, then the top teams and latest events.
options.risk: It's an overview first; full rankings sit one click deeper.

options.label: Season spine
options.thesis: Events in date order are the spine; each one shows its podiums and team medal count, and rankings sit in a tab.
options.viewport: A month index on the left; on the right, event cards with date, place, athlete count, the medal tally, the top team and the leading podiums.
options.risk: Rankings, the main thing asked for, become secondary.
